issue_context.title: LibraryImportGenerator does not respect C# 11 `scoped` modifier on parameters
issue_context.body:
### Description

A `scoped` modifier applied to a P/Invoke attributed with `[LibraryImport(...)]` is not replicated to the generated marshaling method.

### Reproduction Steps

```csharp
[LibraryImport("c", SetLastError = true)]
public static partial nint read(int fildes, scoped Span<byte> buf, nuint nbyte);
```


### Expected behavior

```csharp
[System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCodeAttribute("Microsoft.Interop.LibraryImportGenerator", "7.0.6.47203")]
public static partial nint read(int fildes, scoped global::System.Span<byte> buf, nuint nbyte)
{
    // ...
}
```

### Actual behavior

```csharp
[System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCodeAttribute("Microsoft.Interop.LibraryImportGenerator", "7.0.6.47203")]
public static partial nint read(int fildes, global::System.Span<byte> buf, nuint nbyte)
{
    // ...
}
```

`error CS8988: The 'scoped' modifier of parameter 'buf' doesn't match partial method declaration.`

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

* .NET 7 RC 2
* Windows 11
* x64

### Other information

_No response_

review_comments: We didn't conditionally add this previously, was that a bug?

Technically we were adding a token for `SyntaxKind.None`. That ends up being an empty string when we stringify everything, so it didn't do anything wrong, but it's not necessary (and we get marginally better formatting by not including it when not needed)
Oh, we were just propagating details from the current declaration. This make sense.
